11:1.headline: 'The people' versus 'My people'
11:1.body: Rashi says that when Scripture calls Israel just 'the people', it marks them as doing wrong. When they are good, God calls them 'My people'.

sources.quote: אין העם אלא רשעים
sources.says: Rashi says 'the people' means the wicked.

sources.quote: וכשהם כשרים קרואים "עמי
sources.says: Rashi says that when they are upright they are called 'My people'.

11:1.headline: Complaining, scheming, or grieving?
11:1.body: Rashi says the people were looking for an excuse to turn away from God, and Ibn Ezra hears און, wrongdoing. Ramban says they were in pain and grieving over the hard desert road, and Bekhor Shor hears mourners over the dead.

sources.quote: אין מתאוננים אלא לשון עלילה
sources.says: Rashi says the word means seeking a pretext.

sources.quote: כמתאוננים. מגזרת און
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from און, wrongdoing.

sources.quote: שהוא לשון כואב ומצטער על עצמו
sources.says: Ramban says it means one who is in pain and grieves for himself.

sources.quote: כאוננים על מת
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says they were like mourners over the dead.

11:1.headline: They mumbled so Moses would not hear, but God heard
11:1.body: Rabbeinu Bahya says the people muttered so Moses would not hear them, but God heard. Maimonides says that when the Bible says God heard, it means God knew, and he cites this verse.

sources.quote: ולכך אמר וישמע ה' כלומר ולא משה
sources.says: Bahya says that is why it says God heard, and not Moses.

sources.quote: ביטוי להשגה והוא במשמעות השלישית: "וישמע ה'" (במדבר יא,א ועוד)
sources.says: Maimonides says 'God heard' in this verse means God perceived, in the sense of knowing.

11:1.headline: The fire at the edge: the lowest, or the leaders?
11:1.body: בקצה can mean the edge of the camp, or the people at its edges. Rashi says the fire struck the lowest, the mixed crowd, while Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya hears קצינים, the leaders.

sources.quote: במקצין שבהם לשפלות, אלו ערב רב
sources.says: Rashi says it means those set apart for lowliness, the mixed crowd.

sources.quote: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא אומר, בקצינים שבהם ובגדולים
sources.says: Rashi quotes Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: it means their chiefs and great ones.

11:5.headline: Fish 'for free' in Egypt?
11:5.body: Rashi asks how fish could be free when Egypt would not even give them straw, and answers: 'free' of commandments. Ibn Ezra says it just means cheap, and Ramban says Egyptian fishermen paid them in fish for hauling nets.

sources.quote: ומהו אומר חנם, חנם מן המצות
sources.says: Rashi says 'free' means free of the commandments.

sources.quote: בזול כאילו היא חנם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was so cheap it was as if free.

sources.quote: כי היו הדיגים המצריים מעבידין אותן למשך הדגים
sources.says: Ramban says Egyptian fishermen made them haul in the fish, and paid them with some of the catch.

11:5.headline: Five foods the manna would not taste like
11:5.body: Rabbi Shimon, quoted by Rashi, says the manna could taste like any food except these five. They are bad for nursing mothers, so God left them out.

sources.quote: מפני מה המן משתנה לכל דבר חוץ מאלו? מפני שהן קשים למניקות
sources.says: Rashi quotes Rabbi Shimon: the manna changed into every taste except these, because they are hard on nursing mothers.

11:7.headline: The people complain, and the Torah praises the manna
11:7.body: Right after the people say 'nothing but this manna', the Torah describes how fine it was. Rashi says the speaker has changed: Israel complained, and God wrote its praise so the world would see what they complained about.

sources.quote: מי שאמר זה לא אמר זה
sources.says: Rashi says the one who said this did not say that.

sources.quote: ראו באי עולם על מה מתלוננים בני
sources.says: Rashi says God is telling the world: see what My children complain about.

11:8.headline: Strolling out for food, or roaming to find it?
11:8.body: Rashi says שטו means strolling: they gathered it with no effort. Ibn Ezra reads it as roaming about, which shows the manna fell scattered, not in one heap.

sources.quote: אין שיוט אלא לשון טיול
sources.says: Rashi says the word means strolling.

sources.quote: מגזרת משוט בארץ וזה יורה כי לא היה נופל זה עם זה רק מפוזר ומפורד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is from 'roaming the earth', showing the manna did not fall together but scattered.

11:8.headline: Oil, breast, or three words in one?
11:8.body: Dunash, cited by Rashi, says לשד means the moisture of oil. The sages heard שד, a breast, and another reading splits it into three words: dough kneaded with oil and honey.

sources.quote: לחלוח של שמן, כך פרשו דונש
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash explains it as the moisture of oil.

sources.quote: ורבותינו פרשוהו לשון שדים
sources.says: Rashi says the sages explained it from שד, breasts.

sources.quote: לשד לשון נוטריקון — ליש שמן דבש
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: לשד is short for 'kneaded, oil, honey'.

11:10.headline: Weeping in families, or over family matters?
11:10.body: Rashi first reads it plainly: families gathered to weep in public. The sages read 'over family matters': they wept over the marriages now forbidden to them.

sources.quote: משפחות משפחות נאספים ובוכים לפרסם תרעמתן בגלוי
sources.says: Rashi says family by family they gathered and wept, to make their complaint public.

sources.quote: על עסקי משפחות —על עריות הנאסרות להם
sources.says: Rashi quotes the sages: over family matters, the relations now forbidden to them.

11:12.headline: 'Did I conceive this people?' Moses as father, or as mother
11:12.body: Onkelos reads it 'Am I their father?', since a father is called הורה. Others read it 'Did I conceive them?', as a mother, and Ramban says the whole picture is of a mother.

sources.quote: האב אנא לכל עמא הדין
sources.says: Onkelos translates: am I the father of all this people?

sources.quote: ובעלי הפשט אמרו בהפך: האנכי אמם שהייתי הרה בהם
sources.says: Ramban says the plain-sense commentators read the opposite: am I their mother who was pregnant with them?

sources.quote: ועל דעתי הכל מליצה באם
sources.says: Ramban says in his view the whole image is about a mother.

11:15.headline: Moses speaks to God with a word for a woman
11:15.body: Moses says את, a form of 'you' usually used for a woman. Rashi says his strength had drained away like a woman's, Ibn Ezra says the word works for a man too, and Chizkuni says Moses was sighing and could not finish the word.

sources.quote: תשש כחו של משה כנקבה
sources.says: Rashi says Moses' strength weakened like a woman's.

sources.quote: את. לשון זכר ונקבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says את is used for both male and female.

sources.quote: ולא היה יכול לגמור הדבר ולומר אתה ואמר את כאדם המתאנח
sources.says: Chizkuni says he could not finish saying אתה and said את, like a person sighing.

11:15.headline: 'My evil' may stand for 'their evil'
11:15.body: Rashi says Moses meant 'let me not see their evil', the people's punishment, but the text was softened to 'my evil', one of the scribes' corrections. Ibn Ezra says no correction is needed: Moses means his own suffering.

sources.quote: ברעתם היה לו לכתב, אלא שכנה הכתוב, וזה אחד מתקוני סופרים
sources.says: Rashi says it should have said 'their evil', but the verse softened it, one of the scribes' corrections.

sources.quote: עוד ברעה שאני בה ואין צורך לתקון הסופרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the trouble Moses himself is in, with no need for a scribal correction.

11:16.headline: The officers who took beatings in Egypt now rise
11:16.body: Rashi says these were the Israelite officers in Egypt, who were beaten rather than drive the people harder. Now they are raised up, as they shared the people's pain.

sources.quote: שנתמנו עליהם שוטרים במצרים בעבודת פרך והיו מרחמים עליהם ומכים על ידם
sources.says: Rashi says they were officers over the hard labor in Egypt, who pitied the people and were beaten for it.

sources.quote: עתה יתמנו בגדלתן כדרך שנצטערו בצרתן
sources.says: Rashi says now they are appointed in the people's greatness, as they suffered in their distress.

11:18.headline: 'Make yourselves holy' means 'get ready for punishment'
11:18.body: התקדשו usually means 'make yourselves holy'. Rashi says here it means 'get ready for punishment', as in Jeremiah's 'set them apart for the day of slaughter'.

sources.quote: הזמינו עצמכם לפרענות, וכן הוא אומר (ירמיהו י"ב) "והקדשם ליום הרגה
sources.says: Rashi says it means ready yourselves for punishment, as Jeremiah says 'set them apart for the day of slaughter'.

sources.quote: נמצא לשבח ולגנאי לשון התקדש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is used for good and for bad.

11:20.headline: Meat until it becomes loathsome
11:20.body: זרא appears only here. Ibn Ezra ties it to זר, strange, something loathsome, while Rashi cites Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan that one language calls a sword זרא.

sources.quote: הוא דבר זר נתעב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is something strange and loathsome.

sources.quote: שתהיו מרחקין אותו יותר ממה שקרבתם
sources.says: Rashi says you will push it away more than you drew it near.

sources.quote: ובדברי רבי משה הדרשן ראיתי שיש לשון שקורין לחרב זרא
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan that there is a language that calls a sword זרא.

11:25.headline: The elders prophesied once, or never stopped?
11:25.body: ולא יספו can mean 'they did not do it again' or 'they did not stop'. The Sifrei, in Rashi, says they prophesied only that day, while Onkelos says their prophecy never ceased.

sources.quote: לא נתנבאו אלא אותו היום לבדו
sources.says: Rashi says they prophesied only on that day.

sources.quote: ואנקלוס תרגם "ולא פסקין", שלא פסקה נבואה מהם
sources.says: Rashi notes Onkelos translates 'they did not stop', meaning their prophecy did not cease.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Prefatory Remarks 12
sources.quote: ויש מהם (=מהנביאים) מי שהבריק לו פעם אחת בכל לילו
sources.says: Maimonides says some prophets saw the flash only once in their whole night, and gives this verse.

11:28.headline: Wear them out, or lock them up?
11:28.body: Rashi gives two readings: from כלה, 'load them with public duties and they will wear out', or from כלא, 'put them in prison'. They were prophesying that Moses would die and Joshua would bring Israel into the land.

sources.quote: הטל עליהם צרכי צבור והם כלים מאליהם
sources.says: Rashi says: put the public's needs on them and they will wear out by themselves.

sources.quote: תנם אל בית הכלא, לפי שהיו מתנבאים משה מת ויהושע מכניס את ישראל לארץ
sources.says: Rashi says: put them in prison, because they prophesied that Moses would die and Joshua would bring Israel into the land.

11:28.headline: Joshua: Moses' servant from youth, or his chosen one?
11:28.body: Rashbam reads 'from his youth': Joshua had served Moses since he was young. Ibn Ezra reads 'one of his chosen ones', since Moses had other attendants.

sources.quote: מבחוריו - מנעוריו
sources.says: Rashbam says it means from his youth.

sources.quote: והנכון בעיני שהוא מבחוריו הוא מהמובחרים לשרת משה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means one of those chosen to serve Moses.

11:31.headline: The wind made the quail fly, or sheared them off?
11:31.body: Rashi reads ויגז as 'made them fly', as in 'it passes swiftly'. Ibn Ezra reads it as 'cut off', like shearing: the wind cut away a share of the quail crowded on the shore.

sources.quote: ויגז. ויפריח, וכן "כי גז חיש
sources.says: Rashi says ויגז means made them fly, as in 'for it passes swiftly'.

sources.quote: ויגז. כרת כמו גזי נזרך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means cut off, like 'cut off your hair'.

11:33.headline: Before the meat ran out, or before they could bite it?
11:33.body: Onkelos reads 'before it ran out'. Another reading in Rashi: before they could even bite through the meat, they died.

sources.quote: כתרגומו "עד לא פסק"; ד"א, אינו מספיק לפסקו בשניו עד שנשמתו יוצאה
sources.says: Rashi gives Onkelos' 'before it stopped', and another reading: he could not bite it through before his soul left him.

13:2.headline: "Send for yourself": the mission was Moses' choice, not God's command
13:2.body: God says שלח לך, "send for yourself". Rashi reads the extra word as "by your own judgment": God does not command the spies, He only allows them.

sources.quote: לְדַעְתְּךָ, אֲנִי אֵינִי מְצַוֶּה לְךָ, אִם תִּרְצֶה שְׁלַח
sources.says: Rashi says it means "by your own understanding; I am not commanding you; if you want, send".

13:3.headline: "Men" here means men of standing, still good at the start
13:3.body: The verse calls the spies אנשים, "men". Rashi says the word always marks people of importance, and that at that moment they were still worthy.

sources.quote: כָּל אֲנָשִׁים שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְשׁוֹן חֲשִׁיבוּת, וְאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה כְּשֵׁרִים הָיוּ
sources.says: Rashi says every use of אנשים in Scripture means importance, and at that hour they were worthy.

13:4.headline: Shammua, "one who hears", is the spy who would not listen
13:4.body: The Talmud says the spies were named for what they did. A midrash reads Shammua's name, from "to hear", as a sign that he did not listen to God's words.

sources.quote: מְרַגְּלִים עַל שֵׁם מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם נִקְרְאוּ
sources.says: The Talmud passes on a tradition that the spies were named for their deeds.

sources.quote: על שם שלא שמע לדברי המקום
sources.says: The midrash says Shammua was named for not listening to God's words.

13:13.headline: Sethur, from "tear down", undid God's work
13:13.body: The Talmud reads סתור from the root "to tear down": this spy tore down God's deeds. His father's name מיכאל is read as מך, "lowly", because he made himself small.

sources.quote: שֶׁסָּתַר מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא. ״מִיכָאֵל״ — שֶׁעָשָׂה עַצְמוֹ מָךְ
sources.says: The Talmud says Sethur means he tore down God's deeds, and Michael means he made himself lowly.

13:14.headline: Nahbi, "hidden", is the spy who hid God's words
13:14.body: Rabbi Yohanan reads נחבי from "to hide": he hid God's words. His father's name ופסי is read as "he stepped over" God's ways.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֶחְבִּיא דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא. ״וׇפְסִי״ — שֶׁפִּיסַּע עַל מִדּוֹתָיו
sources.says: The Talmud says Nahbi means he hid God's words and Vophsi means he stepped over God's attributes.

13:16.headline: One added letter turns Hoshea into a prayer
13:16.body: Moses renames Hoshea as Yehoshua by adding a letter. Rashi reads the new name as a prayer, "may God save you from the spies' plan". Rashbam says the renaming happened earlier, when Joshua became Moses' aide.

sources.quote: הִתְפַּלֵּל עָלָיו יָהּ יוֹשִׁיעֲךָ מֵעֲצַת מְרַגְּלִים
sources.says: Rashi says Moses prayed for him: may God save you from the spies' advice.

sources.quote: לא עתה קרא אותו כן, שהרי כבר קודם לכן נקרא יהושע
sources.says: Rashbam says Moses did not name him now, since he was already called Yehoshua before.

13:17.headline: Start with the Negev, the worst part, like a merchant
13:17.body: Moses tells the spies to go up first through the Negev, the dry south. Rashi says it was the poorest part of the land, and a merchant shows his worst goods first.

sources.quote: הוּא הָיָה הַפְּסֹלֶת שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכֵּן דֶּרֶךְ הַתַּגָּרִים מַרְאִין אֶת הַפְּסֹלֶת תְּחִלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says the Negev was the worst of the land, and merchants show the worst first.

13:19.headline: "Camps" means open towns without walls
13:19.body: Moses asks if the cities are במחנים, "in camps", or fortified. Rashi, following Onkelos, says it means open towns with no wall. A people living in open towns trusts its own strength.

sources.quote: כְּרַכִּין פְּצוּחִין וּפְתוּחִין מֵאֵין חוֹמָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word means open cities without a wall.

sources.quote: אִם בִּפְרָזִים יוֹשְׁבִין, חֲזָקִים הֵם, שֶׁסּוֹמְכִין עַל גְּבוּרָתָם
sources.says: Rashi says people who live in open towns are strong, since they rely on their might.

13:20.headline: "Are there trees?" can also ask "is there a good person?"
13:20.body: Moses asks whether the land has עץ, a tree. Sforno takes it plainly: the vines, figs and olives. Rashi reads "tree" as a righteous person whose merit protects the people there.

sources.quote: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אָדָם כָּשֵׁר שֶׁיָּגֵן עֲלֵיהֶם בִּזְכוּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it asks whether there is a worthy person among them who protects them by his merit.

sources.quote: גֶּפֶן וּתְאֵנָה וְרִמּוֹן זֵית שֶׁמֶן וּדְבַשׁ
sources.says: Sforno says it means the fruit trees the land is praised for: vine, fig, pomegranate, olive oil and honey.

13:26.headline: They went out the same way they came back
13:26.body: The verse says "they went and they came" to Moses, though they were only coming back. Rashi says "went" is there to compare the two: they set out with the same bad plan they returned with.

sources.quote: לְהַקִּישׁ הֲלִיכָתָן לְבִיאָתָן, מַה בִּיאָתָן בְּעֵצָה רָעָה אַף הֲלִיכָתָן בְּעֵצָה רָעָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word compares their going to their return: both were with evil intent.

13:30.headline: Caleb said "Shh!" to the crowd
13:30.body: ויהס means Caleb hushed the people. Rashi links it to הס, "hush", and notes people still quiet a crowd with a hissing sound.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן שְׁתִיקָה, וְכֵן "הַס כָּל בָּשָׂר"
sources.says: Rashi says the word means silence, like "hush, all flesh" in Zechariah.

sources.quote: הָרוֹצֶה לְשַׁתֵּק אֲגֻדַּת אֲנָשִׁים אוֹמֵר "שי"ט"
sources.says: Rashi says someone who wants to quiet a group of people makes a hissing sound.

13:31.headline: "Stronger than us" can be read "stronger than Him"
13:31.body: The spies say the people are חזק ממנו, "stronger than us". The same word can mean "than him", and the Talmud reads it that way: they claimed the people were too strong even for God.

sources.quote: כִּבְיָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא כֵּלָיו מִשָּׁם
sources.says: The Talmud reads "than Him": as it were, even the owner cannot take his things out of there.

sources.quote: כִּבְיָכוֹל כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה אָמְרוּ
sources.says: Rashi says they said it, as it were, about God above.

13:32.headline: A land that "eats its people": funerals, or bad air?
13:32.body: The spies say the land "eats" those who live in it. Ibn Ezra takes it as unhealthy air. Rashi says they saw funerals everywhere, which God had arranged so the people would be too busy to notice the spies.

sources.quote: בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁעָבַרְנוּ מְצָאנוּם קוֹבְרֵי מֵתִים, וְהַקָּבָּ"ה עָשָׂה לְטוֹבָה, כְּדֵי לְטָרְדָם בְּאֶבְלָם
sources.says: Rashi says everywhere they passed they found people burying the dead, which God did for their good, to keep the locals busy mourning.

sources.quote: אכלת יושביה. שהאויר שלה רע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the land's air is bad.

13:32.headline: "Men of measures": so big you give their height
13:32.body: The spies call the people אנשי מדות, "men of measures". Rashi says they were so tall that people quote their size, as the Bible does for Goliath.

sources.quote: גְּדוֹלִים וּגְבוֹהִים, וְצָרִיךְ לָתֵת לָהֶם מִדָּה, כְּגוֹן גָּלְיָת
sources.says: Rashi says they were big and tall, and one has to state their measure, like Goliath.

13:33.headline: Anak: giants so tall they wore the sun like a necklace
13:33.body: ענק also means a necklace. Rashi, from the Talmud, says the sons of Anak were so tall that the sun seemed to hang at their necks.

sources.quote: שֶׁמַּעֲנִיקִים חַמָּה בְּקוֹמָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says they "necklace" the sun with their height.

sources.quote: שמעניקין את החמה בקומתם מרוב גובה קומתן
sources.says: Chizkuni repeats Rashi: they wear the sun like a necklace because they are so tall.

15:3.headline: A vow set apart: Ibn Ezra links לפלא to והפלה
15:3.body: Ibn Ezra reads לפלא as to spell out a vow, the same root as והפלה, God will set apart, even though that word is spelled with ה. Onkelos also translates it as setting apart a vow.

sources.quote: לפלא. לפרש וכן והפלה ה' ואם הוא בה"א כי אותיות אהו"י מתחלפות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says לפלא means to spell out, like והפלה, because the letters א and ה can swap.

sources.quote: לְאַפְרָשָׁא נִדְרָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as to set apart a vow.

15:10.headline: Is the wine a fire offering? Rashi and Ralbag disagree
15:10.body: אשה means an offering given to the fire. Rashi says the word covers only the flour and oil, since the wine is not put on the fire, but Ralbag says the wine counts too.

sources.quote: אֵינוֹ מוּסָב אֶלָּא עַל הַמִּנְחָה וְהַשֶּׁמֶן, אֲבָל הַיַּיִן אֵינוֹ אִשֶּׁה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִתָּן עַל הָאֵשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says the word refers only to the flour offering and the oil, not the wine, because wine is not put on the fire.

sources.ref: Ralbag Beur HaMilot on Torah, Numbers 15:10:1
sources.quote: למדנו שהיין בכללו היה אשה ריח ניחוח ליי'
sources.says: Ralbag says we learn that the wine is also included as a fire offering of pleasing smell.

15:22.headline: Failing all the commandments means one sin: idol worship
15:22.body: The verse speaks of failing to do all these commandments. Rashi, following the Sifrei, says it means idol worship, the one sin that equals breaking them all, since it throws off the yoke and breaks the covenant.

sources.quote: בַּעֲ"זָ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says the verse is speaking of idol worship.

sources.quote: מִצְוָה אַחַת שֶׁהִיא כְּכָל הַמִּצְוֹת, מַה הָעוֹבֵר עַל כָּל הַמִּצְוֹת פּוֹרֵק עֹל וּמֵפֵר בְּרִית
sources.says: Rashi says it is one commandment that equals all of them: like one who breaks them all, it throws off the yoke and breaks the covenant.

15:24.headline: A sin offering missing its א, because here it comes second
15:24.body: Here the word for sin offering is spelled without its א. Rashi says this one is unlike the others: everywhere else the sin offering comes before the burnt offering, but here the burnt offering comes first.

sources.quote: חָסֵר א', שֶׁאֵינוֹ כִשְׁאָר חַטָּאוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it lacks an א because it is not like other sin offerings.

sources.quote: הַחַטָּאת קוֹדֶמֶת לָעוֹלָה
sources.says: Rashi says that elsewhere the sin offering comes before the burnt offering.

sources.quote: וְזוֹ עוֹלָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְחַטָּאת
sources.says: Rashi says here the burnt offering comes before the sin offering.

15:30.headline: A raised hand means sinning on purpose, for all to see
15:30.body: Rashi reads ביד רמה, with a raised hand, as on purpose. Onkelos translates it with head uncovered, and Ibn Ezra says it means showing everyone he does not fear God.

sources.quote: ביד רמה. בְמֵזִיד
sources.says: Rashi says it means on purpose.

sources.quote: דְּיַעְבֵּד בְּרֵישׁ גְּלִי
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as one who acts with head uncovered.

sources.quote: ביד רמה להראות הכל שאיננו ירא מהשם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means to show everyone that he does not fear God.

15:30.headline: Reviling God pictured as scraping a bowl clean
15:30.body: Rashi says מגדף means one who reviles. The midrash hears גדף like scraping a bowl: such a person scrapes it clean and leaves nothing in it.

sources.quote: מגדף. מְחָרֵף
sources.says: Rashi says it means one who reviles.

sources.quote: למה עובדי עבודה זרה דומין לאחד שנטל קערה וגדפה ולא שייר הימינה כלום
sources.says: Sifrei Zuta compares idol worshippers to someone who took a bowl, scraped it, and left nothing in it.

sources.quote: איסי בן יהודה אומר כאדם שאומר לחברו גרפת את כל הקערה כולה ולא שיירת ממנה כלום
sources.says: In the Sifrei, Isi ben Yehudah compares it to telling a friend: you scraped the whole bowl and left nothing in it.

15:31.headline: His sin still in him: cut off only if he never repents
15:31.body: Rashi reads עונה בה as while his sin is still in him, meaning he has not repented. Ramban adds the plain sense: he carries his own guilt, like their blood is on them.

sources.quote: בִּזְמַן שֶׁעֲוֹנָהּ בָּהּ — שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה תְשׁוּבָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means while the sin is in him, that is, he did not repent.

sources.quote: וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ הַפְּשָׁט הוּא כְּמוֹ ״דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם״
sources.says: Ramban says that in the plain sense it is like the phrase their blood is on them.

15:33.headline: A word for gathering straw, read as from the line of six
15:33.body: Rabbeinu Bahya asks why the Torah uses מקשש, a word for gathering straw, and not a word for gathering wood. He reads it as מקו ששה, from the line of six: the man treated Shabbat like the six weekdays.

sources.quote: ועוד למה נקרא בלשון מקושש היה לומר מלקט עצים בשבת, כי לשון קשישה אינו נופל כי אם על תבן וקש
sources.says: Bahya asks why it says מקושש and not מלקט, since קשישה is used only for straw.

sources.quote: ועשה הקדש חול והשבת כשאר הששה, ועל כן נקרא מקושש כלומר מקו ששה
sources.says: Bahya says the man made the holy day ordinary, like the other six, so he is called מקושש, meaning from the line of six.

15:34.headline: They knew he must die, but not how
15:34.body: The verse says it was not yet spelled out what to do to him. Rashi says the open question was only which death: they already knew that breaking Shabbat carried death.

sources.quote: בְּאֵיזוֹ מִיתָה יָמוּת, אֲבָל יוֹדְעִים הָיוּ שֶׁמְּחַלֵּל שַׁבָּת בְּמִיתָה
sources.says: Rashi says they did not know by which death he would die, but they knew that one who breaks Shabbat is put to death.

15:39.headline: Do not scout after your heart: the verb used for the spies
15:39.body: תתורו is the verb used for the spies who scouted the land in Numbers 13. Rashi says the heart and eyes are the body's spies: the eye sees, the heart desires, and the body does the sin.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ "מִתּוּר הָאָרֶץ"
sources.says: Rashi says the word is like from scouting the land.

sources.quote: הַלֵּב וְהָעֵינַיִם הֵם מְרַגְּלִים לַגּוּף
sources.says: Rashi says the heart and the eyes are spies for the body.

sources.quote: הָעַיִן רוֹאָה וְהַלֵּב חוֹמֵד וְהַגּוּף עוֹשֶׂה אֶת הָעֲבֵרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the eye sees, the heart desires and the body commits the sin.

15:40.headline: Say the ז clearly, or remember turns into get paid
15:40.body: The sages taught that in reading the Shema one must sound the ז of תזכרו sharply. Bahya explains that said loosely it sounds like תשכרו, you will be paid, and the commandments are not to be done for a reward.

sources.quote: צריך להתיז זי"ן של תזכרו
sources.says: Bahya cites the sages that one must pronounce the ז of תזכרו sharply.

sources.quote: ושלא יובן מזה תשכרו בשי"ן שהוא לשון שכירות לפי שאין לעשות המצות על מנת לקבל פרס
sources.says: Bahya says this is so it will not be heard as תשכרו, about wages, since the commandments are not done to get a reward.

15:41.headline: Two names of God, two promises: reward and punishment
15:41.body: Rashi reads the names one by one. The name יהוה means God is faithful to pay a reward, and אלהיכם, your God, means God is faithful to punish.

sources.quote: נֶאֱמָן לְשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר
sources.says: Rashi says I am the Lord means faithful to pay a reward.

sources.quote: אלהיכם. נֶאֱמָן לִפָּרַע
sources.says: Rashi says your God means faithful to punish.

17:5.headline: "By Moses' hand" recalls the hand that turned leprous
17:5.body: The verse says God spoke "by the hand of Moses", not "to Moses". Rashi brings a midrash: it hints that people who fight over the priesthood are struck with leprosy, as Moses' own hand once was.

sources.quote: וּמַהוּ "בְיַד מֹשֶׁה" וְלֹא כָתַב "אֶל מֹשֶׁה"? רֶמֶז לַחוֹלְקִים עַל הַכְּהֻנָּה שֶׁלּוֹקִין בְּצָרַעַת כְּמוֹ שֶׁלָּקָה מֹשֶׁה בְּיָדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi asks why it says "by the hand of Moses" and answers that it hints at leprosy for those who dispute the priesthood, like Moses' hand.

sources.quote: רמז על החולקים על הכהונה שלוקין בצרעת כשם שלקה משה בצרעת בידו
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya gives the same reading: a hint that those who dispute the priesthood get leprosy, as Moses did in his hand.

17:11.headline: "The fury" read as the name of an angel
17:11.body: The verse says "the fury has gone out from before God". Rabbeinu Bahya reads קצף, "fury", as the name of an angel, a force of God's strict justice, and that is why the plague began.

sources.quote: מלאך יש ששמו קצף, ענף וכח נמשך ממדת הדין, ולכך החל הנגף
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says there is an angel named Ketzef, a force drawn from strict justice, and so the plague began.

17:21.headline: Aaron's rod sat in the middle, so no one could object
17:21.body: Moses put Aaron's rod in the middle of the others. Rashi says this was so no one could claim it blossomed because it lay closest to God's presence.

sources.quote: הִנִּיח בָּאֶמְצַע, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִנִּיחוֹ בְצַד שְׁכִינָה פָּרַח
sources.says: Rashi says Moses put it in the middle so people would not say it blossomed because it was placed beside the Shekhinah.

17:23.headline: The blossom hints at the priests who will come
17:23.body: Young priests were called פרחי כהונה, "blossoms of the priesthood". Chizkuni reads the blossom on Aaron's rod as a sign of those priests who would descend from him.

sources.quote: ויצא פרח סימן לפרחי כהונה העתידין לצאת ממנו
sources.says: Chizkuni says the blossom is a sign of the "blossoms of the priesthood" who would come from Aaron.

17:23.headline: Almonds: the fruit of watchfulness and of speed
17:23.body: Rashi says the almond blossoms faster than any fruit, so punishment comes fast to anyone who fights the priesthood. Ibn Ezra and Rabbeinu Bahya hear שוקד, "watchful", inside שקדים, as in Jeremiah's almond branch.

sources.quote: הוּא הַפְּרִי הַמְמַהֵר לְהַפְרִיחַ מִכָּל הַפֵּרוֹת, אַף הַמְעוֹרֵר עַל הַכְּהֻנָּה פֻּרְעֲנוּתוֹ מְמַהֶרֶת לָבֹא
sources.says: Rashi says the almond blossoms quickest, and so the punishment of one who challenges the priesthood comes quickly.

sources.quote: ודרך דרש כי שקדים כמו כי שוקד אני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes a sermon-style reading that links שקדים to "for I am watchful".

sources.quote: ומפני זה נקראו שקדים מלשון שקידה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says almonds are called שקדים from the word for diligence or watchfulness.

17:27.headline: Three cries of death, one for each disaster
17:27.body: The people cry "we perish, we are lost, all of us are lost". Rabbeinu Bahya matches the words to the three disasters: the burning, the earth swallowing Korah, and the plague. Onkelos even turns גוענו into "the sword killed us".

sources.quote: ויאמר הן גוענו בשרפה, אבדנו בבליעה, הוא שכתוב ויאבדו מתוך הקהל, כלנו אבדנו במגפה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says "we perish" means the burning, "we are lost" the swallowing, and "all of us are lost" the plague.

sources.quote: הָא מִנָּנָא קְטָלַת חַרְבָּא הָא מִנָּנָא בְּלַעַת אַרְעָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: some of us the sword killed, some of us the earth swallowed.

22:5.headline: Petor: a town, or a hint at what Balaam did
22:5.body: In the plain sense פתורה is the name of Balaam's town. The midrash hears more: Rashi compares it to a money-changer's table where kings sent their letters, and Rabbeinu Bahya hears פתרון, interpreting, since Balaam began as an interpreter of dreams.

sources.quote: כְּשֻׁלְחָנִי זֶה שֶׁהַכֹּל מְרִיצִין לוֹ מָעוֹת, כָּךְ כָּל הַמְּלָכִים מְרִיצִין לוֹ אִגְּרוֹתֵיהֶם, וּלְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ שֶׁל מִקְרָא כָּךְ שֵׁם הַמָּקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says that like a money-changer to whom everyone hurries with coins, all kings hurried their letters to him, but in the plain sense it is the place's name.

sources.quote: נקרא פתורה מלשון פתרון, לפי שמתחלה היה פותר חלומות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the midrash reads it as from 'interpretation', because at first he interpreted dreams.

22:11.headline: Balaam makes Balak's curse sharper
22:11.body: Balak asked Balaam to curse Israel with the word ארה. Retelling it, Balaam says קבה instead, which Rashi calls harsher: it means to pierce, to curse by naming outright.

sources.quote: קבה לי. זוֹ קָשָׁה מֵאָרָה לִּי, שֶׁהוּא נוֹקֵב וּמְפָרֵשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says קבה is harsher than 'curse for me', because it pierces and names explicitly.

22:19.headline: 'You too': Balaam's own words predict his failure
22:19.body: Balaam tells the second envoys to stay the night 'you too'. Rashi says his mouth tripped him: you too will go home disappointed, like the first ones.

sources.quote: פִּיו הִכְשִׁילוֹ — גַּם אַתֶּם סוֹפְכֶם לֵילֵךְ בְּפַחֵי נֶפֶשׁ כָּרִאשׁוֹנִים
sources.says: Rashi says his mouth tripped him up: you too will end up leaving disappointed, like the first group.

22:28.headline: 'Three times', or 'three festivals'
22:28.body: The donkey says 'you have struck me three רגלים', three times. Rashi hears the word for the three pilgrimage festivals: you want to uproot a nation that celebrates three festivals a year?

sources.quote: רָמַז לוֹ: אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ לַעֲקֹר אֻמָּה הַחוֹגֶגֶת שָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים בַּשָּׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says she hinted to him: you want to uproot a nation that celebrates three pilgrimage festivals a year?

22:32.headline: A rare verb the sages read as three words
22:32.body: ירט is a very rare verb. The sages read its letters as short for 'she feared, she saw, she turned aside'; Rashi's plain reading is that Balaam rushed down a road that angered God, and Ibn Ezra says it means 'twisted'.

sources.quote: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ חַכְמֵי הַמִּשְׁנָה דְּרָשׁוּהוּ נוֹטָרִיקוֹן — יָרְאָה, רָאֲתָה, נָטְתָה
sources.says: Rashi says the sages of the Mishnah read it as an abbreviation: she feared, she saw, she turned aside.

sources.quote: שֶׁחָרַד וּמִהֵר הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁהוּא לְכַעְסִי וּלְהַמְרוֹתִי
sources.says: Rashi says in the plain sense the traveler hurried anxiously along a road that angered God.

sources.quote: כי ירט. הטעם עוות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means twisted.

23:3.headline: Balaam went off alone, to a hilltop, or limping?
23:3.body: שפי is a rare word with no clear meaning. Rashi follows Onkelos, 'alone and in silence', Ibn Ezra reads 'to a bare height', and Rashbam reads 'limping'.

sources.quote: וילך שפי. כתרגומו יחידי, לשון שפי ושקט, שאין עמו אלא שתיקה
sources.says: Rashi says, as Onkelos translates, that he went alone and quietly, with nothing but silence.

sources.quote: והנכון בעיני שהוא מגזרת קול על שפיים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the right reading is from 'a voice on the bare heights': he went up to a high place.

sources.quote: וילך שפי - חגר כמו: ושופו עצמותיו
sources.says: Rashbam says it means limping, from the verse about bones that are crushed.

23:9.headline: Real rocks, or the patriarchs?
23:9.body: Balaam sees Israel 'from the top of the rocks'. Ibn Ezra reads this plainly as the high place where he stood, while Rashi and Bahya bring the midrash that the rocks are the patriarchs, Israel's strong roots.

sources.quote: כי מראש צורים אראנו. כי על השפי היה והוא גבוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Balaam was standing on a high bare hill.

sources.quote: אני מסתכל בראשיתם ובתחלת שרשיהם ואני רואה אותם מיסדים וחזקים כצורים
sources.says: Rashi says Balaam looked at their beginnings and roots and saw them founded and strong as rocks.

sources.quote: וע"ד המדרש צורים אלו האבות, ומגבעות אלו השבטים
sources.says: Bahya brings the midrash that the rocks are the patriarchs and the hills are the tribes.

23:10.headline: Who can count the dust of Jacob?
23:10.body: Ibn Ezra reads 'dust' plainly: Israel is as many as the dust of the earth. Rashi follows Onkelos, who reads it as their small children, and brings a midrash about the many commandments done with earth and dust.

sources.quote: עפר יעקב. הטעם שהוא רב כעפר הארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means Israel is as many as the dust of the earth.

sources.quote: כתרגומו "דעדקיא דבית יעקב"
sources.says: Rashi cites Onkelos, who translates it as the young children of the house of Jacob.

sources.quote: אין חשבון במצות שהם מקימין בעפר
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that the commandments Israel keeps with earth cannot be counted.

23:21.headline: A trumpet blast for the King, or the King's friendship?
23:21.body: תרועה usually means a trumpet blast, and Ibn Ezra and Sforno read it that way. Rashi and Rashbam read it from רע, friend: the King's love dwells among Israel.

sources.quote: ותרועת מלך בו. לשון חבה ורעות
sources.says: Rashi says the word means love and friendship.

sources.quote: ותרועת מלך - ריעות, כמו: איש רעים להתרועע
sources.says: Rashbam says it means friendship, like 'a man of friends'.

sources.quote: ותרועת מלך בו. במחנה ישראל וזה ותקעתם תרועה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the trumpet blast in Israel's camp, as in 'you shall sound a blast'.

sources.quote: בנסוע המחנות הם תוקעים תרועה בנסוע המשכן לשמחה
sources.says: Sforno says it is the trumpet blast sounded in joy when the camps set out with the Tabernacle.

23:21.headline: A curse turned around: כלם became מלך
23:21.body: Bahya reports a tradition that Balaam meant to say כלם, 'destroy them'. God turned the letters around in his mouth, and it came out מלך, King, a curse turned into a blessing.

sources.quote: לפי שהקללה אלמלא שנהפכה היתה כל"ם באותו רגע שהוא שעת הכעס
sources.says: Bahya says that had the curse not been turned around, the word would have been כלם, said at a moment of anger.

sources.quote: נתן בלבו להפך המלה שהיה כלם ואמר מלך
sources.says: Bahya says God put it in Balaam's heart to reverse the word, so instead of כלם he said מלך.

24:2.headline: Each tribe camped apart, no tent door facing another
24:2.body: Rashi says Balaam saw each tribe camped by itself, with tent doors set so no one could look into a neighbor's tent. Rabbeinu Bahya says this sight is what made him cry 'How good are your tents'.

sources.quote: רָאָה כָל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט שׁוֹכֵן לְעַצְמוֹ וְאֵינָן מְעֹרָבִין, רָאָה שֶׁאֵין פִּתְחֵיהֶם מְכֻוָּנִין זֶה כְנֶגֶד זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says he saw each tribe dwelling by itself, unmixed, and that their doors did not face each other.

sources.quote: ראה דגלים מסודרים ושאין פתחיהן מכוונין זה כנגד זה כדי שלא יעשו היזק ראיה זה לזה, מיד אמר מה טובו אוהליך
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says he saw the ordered camps and doors placed so no one would harm another by looking in, and at once said 'How good are your tents'.

24:3.headline: Hagever: Balaam the 'rooster' who knew the hour of God's anger
24:3.body: Rabbeinu Bahya says Balaam called himself גבר because he likened himself to a rooster, which knows the exact hours. Only Balaam among people, and the rooster among birds, could find the moment of God's anger.

sources.quote: קרא עצמו גבר כי המשיל עצמו לתרנגול היודע לכוין השעות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says he called himself gever because he compared himself to the rooster, which knows how to pinpoint the hours.

sources.quote: ואין העולם מי שיוכל לכוין שעת כעסו של הקב"ה כי אם בלעם בבני אדם ותרנגול בעופות
sources.says: He says no one could pinpoint the hour of God's anger except Balaam among people and the rooster among birds.

24:4.headline: 'A vision of Shaddai', not Shaddai itself
24:4.body: Ramban, quoted by Rabbeinu Bahya, says the patriarchs knew God as El Shaddai, while Balaam saw only a 'vision of Shaddai'. Bahya concludes that Balaam stood two levels below the patriarchs.

sources.quote: וכן כתב הרמב"ן ז"ל מחזה שדי אינו שדי, כי האבות באל שדי ובלעם במחזה של שדי
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites Ramban: a vision of Shaddai is not Shaddai; the patriarchs had El Shaddai, Balaam a vision of Shaddai.

sources.quote: אבל היה חסר ממנו שתי מדרגות
sources.says: Bahya says Balaam fell two levels short of the patriarchs.

24:5.headline: 'Your tents': the camp, the Temple, or houses of study?
24:5.body: Rashi first ties the praise to the tents' doors, which did not face each other; he also reads 'your tents' as the Tabernacle at Shiloh and the Temple. Sforno reads them as houses of study.

sources.quote: עַל שֶׁרָאָה פִתְחֵיהֶם שֶׁאֵינָן מְכֻוָּנִין זֶה מוּל זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says he praised them because he saw their doors did not face each other.

sources.quote: מַה טֹּבוּ אֹהֶל שִׁילֹה וּבֵית עוֹלָמִים בְּיִשּׁוּבָן
sources.says: Rashi also reads it: how good are the Tent at Shiloh and the Temple while they stand.

sources.quote: מַה טֹּבוּ אֹהָלֶיךָ יַעֲקֹב. בָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת
sources.says: Sforno says the tents of Jacob are houses of study.

24:5.headline: Mishkenot: dwellings that are also a pledge
24:5.body: Rashi hears משכון, 'a pledge', in משכנות, 'dwellings'. Even when the Temple lies in ruins it is held as a pledge for Israel, and its destruction atones for their lives.

sources.quote: אַף כְּשֶׁהֵן חֲרֵבִין, לְפִי שֶׁהֵן מַשְׁכּוֹן עֲלֵיכֶם, וְחֻרְבָּנָן כַּפָּרָה עַל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they are good even when destroyed, because they are a pledge for you and their ruin atones for your souls.

24:6.headline: Ahalim: one verse after 'tents', the word means aloes
24:6.body: Right after 'your tents' (אהליך), the same word returns as אהלים. Onkelos, Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it as aloes, a fragrant tree, as in 'myrrh and aloes'; Rashi also offers 'like the heavens spread out as a tent'.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ, לְשׁוֹן "מֹר וַאֲהָלוֹת"
sources.says: Rashi follows Onkelos: the word is as in 'myrrh and aloes'.

sources.quote: כְּבוּסְמַיָּא דִּנְצִיב יְיָ
sources.says: Onkelos renders: like spice trees that God planted.

sources.quote: כאהלים. כמו מר ואהלות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra also reads it as aloes.

sources.quote: כַּשָּׁמַיִם הַמְּתוּחִין כְּאֹהֶל
sources.says: Rashi's other reading: like the heavens stretched out as a tent.

24:7.headline: Nisa: Maimonides says this 'lifting' is rank, not height
24:7.body: Maimonides says נשא has two senses: lifting something up in space, and raising in rank. He places 'his kingdom will be lifted up' in the second sense.

sources.quote: וכן יש ל"נשא" א) משמעות של רום המקום, ב) ומשמעות של רוממות הדרגה ויתרון המעלה
sources.says: Maimonides says נשא means either height of place or loftiness of rank.

sources.quote: ובמשמעות השנייה: "וְתִנַּשֵּׂא מַלְכֻתוֹ"
sources.says: He lists 'his kingdom will be exalted' under the second sense.

24:17.headline: Karkar: dig out, or tear down the wall
24:17.body: קרקר is a rare verb. Rashi links it to digging, as in 'I dug (קרתי) wells'; Ibn Ezra links it to tearing down a wall (מקרקר קיר).

sources.quote: וקרקר. לְשׁוֹן קוֹרֶה, כְּמוֹ "אֲנִי קַרְתִּי"
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for digging, as in 'I dug'.

sources.quote: וקרקר. כמו מקרקר קיר והטעם הורס הקיר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like 'battering down a wall', meaning destroying it.

24:17.headline: 'Sons of Shet': all humanity, or the foundations of cities?
24:17.body: Rashi says the sons of Seth are all nations, since all descend from Seth son of Adam. Ibn Ezra cites many who read שת as 'foundations' (השתות), so the verse means he will tear cities down, and calls that plausible.

sources.quote: כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת, שֶׁכֻּלָּם יָצְאוּ מִן שֵׁת בְּנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means all the nations, who all came from Seth son of Adam.

sources.quote: ורבים פירשו כל בני שת מגזרת כי השתות והטעם כי יהרום המדינות ואיננו רחוק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says many derive it from 'the foundations', meaning he will destroy cities, and that this is not far-fetched.

24:20.headline: 'First of nations': first to attack, not first in rank
24:20.body: Rashi and Onkelos read ראשית as 'first': Amalek was the first nation to make war on Israel. Ibn Ezra notes that many read it as 'chief of nations', and rejects that, since Amalek never was.

sources.quote: הוּא קָדַם אֶת כֻּלָּם לְהִלָּחֵם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says Amalek came before all others to fight Israel.

sources.quote: רֵישׁ קְרָבַיָּא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל הֲוָה עֲמַלְקָאָה
sources.says: Onkelos renders: Amalek was the first of the wars of Israel.

sources.quote: ורבים פירשו ראשית גוים כי הם יחשבו בראש הגוים ולא היה כן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says many explained it as Amalek being counted first among nations, but that was not so.

24:21.headline: The Kenite (קיני) told to set his nest (קן) in the rock
24:21.body: Rabbeinu Bahya says the parable speaks of a nest, קן, because the tribe's name is קיני. Even a home set high as a bird's nest will not keep them safe.

sources.quote: ושים בסלע קנך, על שם ששמו קיני הוזכר במשלו קן
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the nest is mentioned in the parable because his name is Keini.

sources.quote: אילו היית משים מושבך החזק גבוה כקן העוף משם תרד
sources.says: He says: even if you set your strong home high like a bird's nest, you will come down from there.

sources.quote: כי אילו היה מושבך גבוה כקן העוף לא יצילך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says even a dwelling high as a bird's nest would not save you.

24:23.headline: El: 'God', or 'these things'?
24:23.body: אל usually means God. Rashi reads it as 'these' (אלה): who can survive when He brings these things about, when Sennacherib throws the nations into chaos; Ibn Ezra offers that it is the king of Assyria, who set himself up as a god.

sources.quote: מִי יָכוֹל לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִשּׂוּמוֹ אֶת אֵלֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says: who can keep himself alive when He sets these things in place.

sources.quote: שֶׁיַּעֲמֹד סַנְחֵרִיב וִיבַלְבֵּל אֶת כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says these things are Sennacherib rising and throwing all nations into confusion.

sources.quote: הטעם על מלך אשור ששם נפשו כמו אל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it refers to the king of Assyria, who made himself like a god.

24:24.headline: Tzim: great ships coming from Kittim
24:24.body: Rashi and Rashbam read צים as great ships, like 'a mighty ship (צי)' in Isaiah. Onkelos renders it as bands of men from Rome.

sources.quote: וצים. סְפִינוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says צים are great ships.

sources.quote: וצים - כמו: וצי אדיר
sources.says: Rashbam compares 'and a mighty ship'.

sources.quote: וְסִיעַן יִצְטָרְחַן מֵרוֹמָאֵי
sources.says: Onkelos renders: and bands will gather from the Romans.

25:1.headline: 'He settled' is a warning that trouble is coming
25:1.body: The chapter opens with וישב, 'Israel settled'. Rabbi Yochanan says that wherever the Torah uses this word, pain follows, and his first proof is this verse: settling at Shittim leads straight into sin.

sources.quote: כל מקום שנאמר ״וישב״ אינו אלא לשון צער, שנאמר: ״וישב ישראל בשטים
sources.says: Rabbi Yochanan says that every place the Torah says 'and he settled' means trouble, and he cites this verse first.

25:1.headline: 'Began', or 'made their holiness ordinary'?
25:1.body: ויחל plainly means the people 'began' to go after Moabite women. Rabbeinu Bahya and Or HaChaim also hear חול, ordinary or profane, in it: the people turned their holiness into something common.

sources.quote: ויחל העם. עשה קדושתו חול, כלשון (בראשית ט׳:כ׳) ויחל נח
sources.says: Bahya says the people made their holiness profane, using the word the same way as 'Noah began' in Genesis.

sources.quote: אמרו ויחל לשון חלול, שנתחלל לזנות
sources.says: Or HaChaim cites the sages that ויחל means profaning: the people profaned themselves by going astray.

25:3.headline: Yoked to Peor, but not stuck to it
25:3.body: ויצמד comes from צמד, a pair of oxen under one yoke. Rabbeinu Bahya says being yoked is a looser bond than cleaving: Israel was attached to Peor like a bracelet on a hand, but cleaves to God for real.

sources.quote: ויצמד ישראל. מגזרת צמד בקר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from a yoked pair of oxen.

sources.quote: ויש חלוק בין לשון הצמדה ולשון דבקות
sources.says: Bahya says there is a difference between being yoked and cleaving.

sources.quote: הנצמדים לבעל פעור כצמידים על ידי אשה, ואתם הדבקים דבקים ממש
sources.says: Bahya quotes the sages: those yoked to Peor were like bracelets on a woman's hand, but those who cleave to God truly cleave.

25:3.headline: Peor is named for its crude form of worship
25:3.body: Rashi links פעור to פער, to open wide. He says the idol was worshipped by people baring themselves before it and relieving themselves, and that this was its service.

sources.quote: על שם שפוערין לפניו פי הטבעת ומוציאין רעי, וזו היא עבודתו
sources.says: Rashi says it is named for the way worshippers exposed themselves and relieved themselves before it, which was its worship.

25:8.headline: An unusual word for a tent that Ibn Ezra hears in Arabic
25:8.body: Rashi says הקבה, where Pinchas followed the man, means the tent. Ibn Ezra agrees and says a close word exists in the language of Kedar, his name for Arabic.

sources.quote: אל הקבה. אל האהל
sources.says: Rashi says the word means the tent.

sources.quote: כמו אל האהל וכן קרוב בלשון קדר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the tent, and a close word exists in the language of Kedar.

25:8.headline: Into the tent, and into her belly
25:8.body: Pinchas enters the קבה, the tent, and stabs the woman אל קבתה, nearly the same word. Rashi reads it as her belly, like the stomach portion given to priests, while Ibn Ezra also records 'in her tent'.

sources.quote: אל קבתה. כמו "והלחיים והקבה"
sources.says: Rashi says the word is the same as the stomach in the list of the priest's portions.

sources.quote: בקובה שהיתה שם עם אחי זמרי. וי"א כי קבתה מגזרת הזרוע והלחיים והקבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives two readings: in the tent where Zimri's brothers were, or the stomach, as in the priest's portions.

sources.quote: הקבה כנגד ואת האשה אל קבתה
sources.says: Bahya says the priests receive the stomach portion as a reward for Pinchas stabbing the woman in her belly.

26:5.headline: God's name wraps each clan name, ה in front, י behind
26:5.body: Each clan name in this list is written with ה before it and י after it. Rashi says these two letters spell God's name, יה, as a witness that every family really comes from its fathers, even after Egypt.

sources.quote: לְפִיכָךְ הִטִּיל הַקָּבָּ"ה שְׁמוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם — ה"א מִצַּד זֶה וְיוֹ"ד מִצַּד זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says God put His name on them, a ה on one side and a י on the other.

sources.quote: לוֹמַר, מֵעִיד אֲנִי עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁהֵם בְּנֵי אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the name testifies that they are the sons of their fathers.

sources.quote: וְחָתַם עֲלֵיהֶם שֵׁם יָ״הּ, כִּי שֵׁם זֶה הוּא מְתַוֵּךְ בֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשָּׁה
sources.says: Kli Yakar says the name יה is sealed on them because it stands between husband and wife.

26:10.headline: לנס: a warning sign, or a banner raised in honor?
26:10.body: Rashi and Ralbag read נס as a sign and a reminder, warning anyone who would fight the priesthood. The Netziv reads it as 'raised high': the rebels' fire pans became plating for the altar.

sources.quote: ויהיו לנס. לְאוֹת וּלְזִכָּרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means a sign and a reminder, so no outsider would again challenge the priesthood.

sources.ref: Ralbag Beur HaMilot on Torah, Numbers 26:10:1
sources.quote: שהיו לאות ולזכרון לבני ישראל להזהירם שלא יקרב איש אשר לא מזרע אהרן
sources.says: Ralbag says they became a sign to warn Israel that no one outside Aaron's family may serve in the sanctuary.

sources.quote: פי׳ גבוה במעלה שזכו לשם טוב במה שצוה הקב״ה לעשות מן המחתות צפוי למזבח
sources.says: The Netziv says it means raised high: they earned a good name when their fire pans were made into the altar's covering.

26:13.headline: Zerah and Tzochar: one man, two names of light
26:13.body: In Genesis this son of Simeon is called צחר. Rashi and Ramban say Zerah is the same man, and explain צחר as צהר, light. זרח also speaks of light: it is the word for the sun rising.

sources.quote: לזרח. הוּא צֹחַר, לְשׁוֹן צֹהַר
sources.says: Rashi says Zerah is Tzochar, a word related to צהר, light.

sources.quote: לְזֶרַח הוּא צוֹחַר (בראשית מו י) לְשׁוֹן צֹהַר
sources.says: Ramban repeats that Zerah is the Tzochar of Genesis, from the word for light.

26:16.headline: Etzbon became Ozni, and both names mean 'listen'
26:16.body: Rashi says the clan of אזני is Gad's son Etzbon from Genesis, but does not know why the name changed. Or HaChaim cites a midrash: both names mean listening, from אצית and האזין, so it is really the same name.

sources.quote: אוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁזּוֹ מִשְׁפַּחַת אֶצְבּוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says this is the family of Etzbon, and he does not know why it is not called by his name.

sources.quote: מִלְּשׁוֹן אֲצֵית וְהֶאֱזִין
sources.says: Or HaChaim quotes the Pesikta that Ozni is Etzbon, both from words meaning to listen.

sources.quote: וְאֵין הַכָּתוּב מַקְפִּיד עַל שִׁנּוּי הַשֵּׁם כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ שֵׁם הָרִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Or HaChaim says Scripture does not mind a changed name when it keeps the first name's meaning.

26:24.headline: Yov becomes Yashuv, borrowing a letter from his father
26:24.body: In Genesis this son of Issachar is called יוב. Chizkuni says he gained a ש from his father's name, יששכר, which has two of them.

sources.quote: לישוב. הוּא יוֹב הָאָמוּר בְּיוֹרְדֵי מִצְרַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says Yashuv is the Yov listed among those who went down to Egypt.

sources.quote: לישוב הוא יוב שנתוספה לו שי״‎ן אחת משני שיני״‎ן שבשם אביו
sources.says: Chizkuni says one of the two letters ש in his father's name was added to Yov's name.

26:38.headline: Achiram: named for a brother who rose high
26:38.body: In Genesis this son of Benjamin is called אחי. Rashi says the name אחירם is for Joseph: Benjamin's brother (אח) who was raised (רם) above him.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי שֶׁנִּקְרָא עַל שֵׁם יוֹסֵף שֶׁהָיָה אָחִיו וְרָם מִמֶּנּוּ נִקְרָא אֲחִירָם
sources.says: Rashi says he was named for Joseph, his brother who was higher than him, so he is called Achiram.

26:44.headline: One clan name already carries God's name inside it
26:44.body: Every other clan here gets ה in front and י at the end. Rashi says ימנה did not need them, since its name already starts with י and ends with ה. Ibn Ezra notes the clan is called הימנה, not הימיני.

sources.quote: אֲבָל בְּיִמְנָה לֹא הֻצְרַךְ לוֹמַר "מִשְׁפַּחַת הַיִּמְנִי" לְפִי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם קָבוּעַ בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says ימנה did not need the extra letters because the name is already fixed in it.

sources.quote: לימנה משפחת הימנה ואיננו הימיני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes the clan of Yimnah is called הימנה, not הימיני.

26:46.headline: Was Serah Asher's daughter, or his wife's?
26:46.body: Rashi says Serah is listed because she was still alive. Ramban reports that Onkelos calls her the daughter of Asher's wife. She was his stepdaughter, so she could inherit land, and that is why she is counted here.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה קַיֶּמֶת בְּחַיֶּיהָ מְנָאָהּ כָּאן
sources.says: Rashi says she was counted here because she was still alive.

sources.quote: אֲבָל הָיְתָה בַּת אִשְׁתּוֹ מֵאִישׁ אַחֵר, לֹא הָיָה לוֹ בֵּן וְהָיְתָה נַחֲלָתוֹ לְבִתּוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says she was Asher's wife's daughter by another man, who had no son, so his land went to her.

sources.quote: לפי שגדלה בתוך ביתו והיתה נקראת על שמו
sources.says: Chizkuni says she was called Asher's daughter because she grew up in his house.

26:55.headline: 'Only by lot': the small word that leaves out Joshua and Caleb
26:55.body: Rashi stops on אך, 'only', a word that limits. He says it leaves out Joshua and Caleb, who got their land by God's word and not by lot.

sources.quote: אך בגורל. יָצְאוּ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָלֵב
sources.says: Rashi says 'only by lot' excludes Joshua and Caleb.

sources.quote: אך יצאו יהושע וכלב שלא נטלו בגורל
sources.says: Chizkuni says אך excludes Joshua and Caleb, who did not take their share by lot.

26:56.headline: 'By the mouth of the lot': the lot itself spoke
26:56.body: על פי usually means 'according to', but פי is also 'mouth'. Rashi says the lot really spoke and called out which tribe got which land. Bekhor Shor reads it as 'by mouth and by lot': the priest named the land, and the lot agreed.

sources.quote: על פי הגורל. הַגּוֹרָל הָיָה מְדַבֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says the lot was speaking.

sources.quote: וְהַגּוֹרָל עַצְמוֹ הָיָה צוֹוֵחַ וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי הַגּוֹרָל עָלִיתִי
sources.says: Rashi says the lot itself cried out, 'I, the lot, came up for this border and this tribe'.

sources.quote: על פי הגורל. על פה וגורל
sources.says: Bekhor Shor reads it as 'by mouth and by lot', the priest speaking and the lot matching.

26:59.headline: Born in Egypt: Yocheved arrived just as the family did
26:59.body: Rashi reads 'born in Egypt' closely: she was conceived before, and born as the family entered Egypt's walls. That makes her the seventieth person who went down. Ralbag says the words do not force this reading.

sources.quote: לֵדָתָהּ בְּמִצְרַיִם וְאֵין הוֹרָתָהּ בְּמִצְרַיִם, כְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ לְתוֹךְ הַחוֹמָה יְלָדַתָּה
sources.says: Rashi says she was born in Egypt but not conceived there; she was born as they came within the walls.

sources.quote: וְהִיא הִשְׁלִימָה מִנְיַן שִׁבְעִים
sources.says: Rashi says she completed the count of seventy.

sources.ref: Ralbag Beur HaMilot on Torah, Numbers 26:59:1
sources.quote: שלא תהיה הורתה גם כן במצרים כמו שלא יחייב אמרו ויולד ליוסף בארץ מצרים
sources.says: Ralbag says the verse does not mean she was not also conceived in Egypt, just as with Joseph's sons born in Egypt.

26:64.headline: 'Not a man was left', but the women were
26:64.body: Rashi reads איש as 'man', not 'person'. The decree after the spies fell only on the men, he says, because the women loved the land and asked for a share in it.

sources.quote: אֲבָל עַל הַנָּשִׁים לֹא נִגְזְרָה גְזֵרַת הַמְרַגְּלִים, לְפִי שֶׁהֵן הָיוּ מְחַבְּבוֹת אֶת הָאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says the spies' decree was not made against the women, because they loved the land.

sources.quote: וּבְאֵלֶּה לֹא הָיָה אִישׁ. אֲבָל נָשִׁים הָיוּ
sources.says: Kli Yakar says no men were left, but women were.

3:1.headline: Moses' 'offspring' are Aaron's sons, because he taught them
3:1.body: The verse promises the offspring of Aaron and Moses but lists only Aaron's sons. Rashi says they count as Moses' too because he taught them Torah: teaching someone's child is like giving birth to him.

sources.quote: וְנִקְרְאוּ תוֹלְדוֹת מֹשֶׁה, לְפִי שֶׁלִּמְּדָן תּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says they are called Moses' offspring because he taught them Torah.

sources.quote: שֶׁכָּל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן חֲבֵרוֹ תּוֹרָה מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ יְלָדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says whoever teaches another's son Torah is regarded by Scripture as if he had fathered him.

sources.quote: כי תלמידיו של אדם הן הן תולדותיו העקריות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says a person's students are his truest offspring.

3:4.headline: 'Al pnei Aharon': in Aaron's lifetime, or before his eyes?
3:4.body: Rashi reads על פני as 'in his lifetime'. Ramban objects that every priest serves in his father's lifetime, and reads it as Nadav and Avihu dying in front of their father, as Chronicles says 'before their father'.

sources.quote: על פני אהרן. בְּחַיָּיו
sources.says: Rashi says 'al pnei Aharon' means in Aaron's lifetime.

sources.quote: כִּי כָל אִישׁ מִבְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים יְכַהֵן בְּחַיֵּי אָבִיו
sources.says: Ramban objects that any son of Aaron serves as priest in his father's lifetime.

sources.quote: וַיָּמָת נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא לִפְנֵי ה' עַל פְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן אֲבִיהֶם בְּהַקְרִיבָם אֵשׁ זָרָה
sources.says: Ramban reads it as: Nadav and Avihu died before God, in front of Aaron their father, when they offered strange fire.

sources.quote: וַיָּמָת נָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא לִפְנֵי אֲבִיהֶם
sources.says: Ramban cites Chronicles: Nadav and Avihu died before their father.

3:10.headline: Tifkod: in a counting chapter, here it means 'appoint'
3:10.body: פקד is the verb for counting all through this chapter. Rashi and Rashbam say that here it means appointing Aaron and his sons to office, as 'the captain of the guard appointed (ויפקד) Joseph'.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן פְּקִידוּת, וְאֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן מִנְיָן
sources.says: Rashi says it means appointment, not counting.

sources.quote: תעשהו פקיד וממונה עליהם. כמו: ויפקד שר הטבחים את יוסף
sources.says: Rashbam says: make him an officer in charge, as in 'the captain of the guard appointed Joseph'.

sources.quote: וְיָת אַהֲרֹן וְיָת בְּנוֹהִי תְּמַנֵּי
sources.says: Onkelos renders: and Aaron and his sons you shall appoint.

3:12.headline: The Levites took the firstborns' place after the golden calf
3:12.body: Rashi says the service first belonged to the firstborn. When they sinned with the golden calf they lost it, and the Levites, who had not worshipped the idol, were chosen in their place.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה הָעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת, וּכְשֶׁחָטְאוּ בָעֵגֶל נִפְסְלוּ, וְהַלְוִיִּם שֶׁלֹּא עָבְדוּ עֲ"זָ נִבְחֲרוּ תַחְתֵּיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the service was with the firstborn; when they sinned with the calf they were disqualified, and the Levites, who did not worship idols, were chosen instead.

sources.quote: מִקֶּדֶם הָיְתָה הָעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Sforno also says the service was once done by the firstborn.

3:15.headline: Levites counted from one month old: why so young
3:15.body: Rashi says that at one month a baby is past the danger of dying as a newborn and can be called a guardian of the holy; a midrash he cites adds that this tribe was counted even from the womb. Rashbam says it matches the firstborn they replace, who are redeemed from one month.

sources.quote: מִשֶּׁיָּצָא מִכְּלַל נְפָלִים הוּא נִמְנֶה לִקָּרֵא שׁוֹמֵר מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says once a baby is past the risk of dying newborn, he is counted and called a keeper of the holy charge.

sources.quote: לָמוּד הוּא אוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁבֶט לִהְיוֹת נִמְנֶה מִן הַבֶּטֶן
sources.says: Rashi cites a midrash that this tribe was used to being counted from the womb.

sources.quote: לפי שהיו באים לפטור את הבכורות שחייבין בפדיון מבן חדש ומעלה, לכן גם מניינם מבן חדש
sources.says: Rashbam says the Levites came to release the firstborn, who are redeemed from one month, so they were counted from one month too.

3:16.headline: Counting babies 'by the mouth of God': a voice from each tent
3:16.body: Moses asked how he could go into people's tents to count their nursing infants. Rashi brings a midrash: Moses stood at each tent door, and a heavenly voice from inside announced how many babies were there.

sources.quote: הֵיאַךְ אֲנִי נִכְנָס לְתוֹךְ אָהֳלֵיהֶם לָדַעַת מִנְיַן יוֹנְקֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says Moses asked how he could enter their tents to know the number of their nursing babies.

sources.quote: וּבַת קוֹל יוֹצְאָה מִן הָאֹהֶל וְאוֹמֶרֶת כָּךְ וָכָךְ תִּינוֹקוֹת יֵשׁ בְּאֹהֶל זֶה, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר עַל פִּי ה'
sources.says: Rashi says a heavenly voice came from the tent saying how many infants were in it, and that is why it says 'by the mouth of God'.

3:31.headline: 'The screen': the inner curtain, or the Tent's door?
3:31.body: Rashi says this מסך is the inner curtain, the פרכת, which is also called 'the curtain of the screen'. Ibn Ezra says many got this wrong: it is the screen at the entrance to the Tent.

sources.quote: הִיא הַפָּרֹכֶת, שֶׁאַף הִיא קְרוּיָה פָּרֹכֶת הַמָּסָךְ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the parochet, which is also called the curtain of the screen.

sources.quote: ורבים השתבשו בפירוש והמסך וכל עבודתו והאמת ברורה שהוא מסך פתח אהל מועד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says many erred in explaining 'the screen'; the truth is that it is the screen at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

3:39.headline: Dots over 'and Aaron': he was not in the Levite count
3:39.body: The word ואהרן here is written with dots over its letters. Rashi says the dots show that Aaron was not part of the count of the Levites.

sources.quote: נָקוּד עַל וְאַהֲרֹן, לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּמִנְיַן הַלְוִיִּם
sources.says: Rashi says there are dots on 'and Aaron' to say he was not among those counted as Levites.

31:3.headline: Not just 'men': here the word means righteous men
31:3.body: Rashi says אנשים here means righteous men, as when Moses told Joshua to 'choose us men'. Ramban explains why that mattered: many had sinned with the women of Moab and were not fit to carry out God's revenge.

sources.quote: אנשים. צַדִּיקִים, וְכֵן "בְּחַר לָנוּ אֲנָשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says 'men' here means righteous men, as in 'choose us men' (Exodus 17).

sources.quote: כִּי הַנִּכְשָׁלִים בִּבְנוֹת מוֹאָב הָיוּ רַבִּים וְאֵינָם רְאוּיִים לְנִקְמַת ה', עַל כֵּן בָּחֲרוּ אֲנָשִׁים צַדִּיקִים וִידוּעִים לְשִׁבְטֵיהֶם
sources.says: Ramban says many had stumbled with the women of Moab and were unfit for God's revenge, so they chose righteous men known to their tribes.

31:3.headline: God calls it Israel's revenge; Moses calls it God's
31:3.body: In verse 2 God says 'avenge the Israelites', but here Moses says 'the LORD's vengeance'. Chizkuni gives Moses' reason: the nations hate Israel only because of God, so the revenge is His.

sources.quote: הקב״‎ה אומר נקמת בני ישראל ומשה אומר נקמת ה׳‎ אמר משה רבונו של עולם הנקמה שלך היא שאין הכנענים שונאים אותנו אלא בשבילך
sources.says: Chizkuni says God said 'Israel's vengeance' and Moses said 'the LORD's vengeance', telling God the revenge is His, since the nations hate Israel only because of Him.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָעוֹמֵד כְּנֶגֶד יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּאִלּוּ עוֹמֵד כְּנֶגֶד הַקָּבָּ"ה
sources.says: Rashi says whoever stands against Israel is as if he stands against God.

31:5.headline: 'Handed over': the soldiers did not want to go
31:5.body: וימסרו means they were handed over, not that they stepped forward. Rashi says the men refused to go because they had heard Moses would die once Midian was punished, so they had to be sent against their will.

sources.quote: וּמִשֶּׁשָּׁמְעוּ שֶׁמִּיתַת מֹשֶׁה תְלוּיָה בְנִקְמַת מִדְיָן לֹא רָצוּ לָלֶכֶת עַד שֶׁנִּמְסְרוּ עַל כָּרְחָן
sources.says: Rashi says once they heard Moses' death depended on the revenge against Midian, they would not go until they were handed over against their will.

sources.quote: וימסרו - בעל כרחן, לפי שאמר הקדוש ברוך הוא: ואחר תאסף אל עמך
sources.says: Rashbam says they went against their will, because God had said Moses would then be gathered to his people.

31:8.headline: Kings who fell out of the sky onto the dead
31:8.body: על חלליהם can mean 'with their slain' or 'on top of their slain'. Rashi tells a midrash: Balaam made Midian's kings fly by sorcery, and when they were shown the gold plate bearing God's name they fell onto the bodies below.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה בִּלְעָם עִמָּהֶם וּמַפְרִיחַ מַלְכֵי מִדְיָן בִּכְשָׁפִים וְהוּא עַצְמוֹ פוֹרֵחַ עִמָּהֶם, הֶרְאָה לָהֶם אֶת הַצִּיץ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם חָקוּק בּוֹ וְהֵם נוֹפְלִים, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר "עַל חַלְלֵיהֶם" בְּמַלְכֵי מִדְיָן — שֶׁנּוֹפְלִים עַל הַחֲלָלִים מִן הָאֲוִיר
sources.says: Rashi says Balaam made the kings of Midian fly by sorcery; shown the headplate engraved with God's name, they fell onto the slain from the air.

sources.quote: על חלליהם עם חלליהם
sources.says: Chizkuni reads it plainly as 'with their slain'.

31:8.headline: Balaam took Israel's weapon, words, so Israel took his
31:8.body: Rashi says Israel wins with its mouth, by prayer, while the nations win with the sword. Balaam tried to beat Israel with his mouth by cursing them, so Israel came against him with the sword.

sources.quote: הוּא בָא עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהֶחֱלִיף אֻמָּנוּתוֹ בְּאֻמָּנוּתָם, שֶׁאֵין נוֹצְחִים אֶלָּא בְּפִיהֶם וְעַל יְדֵי תְפִלָּה וּבַקָּשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says Balaam came against Israel and swapped his craft for theirs, since they win only with their mouths, through prayer and request.

sources.quote: אַף הֵם בָּאוּ עָלָיו וְהֶחֱלִיפוּ אֻמָּנוּתָם בְּאֻמָּנוּת הָאֻמּוֹת שֶׁבָּאִין בַּחֶרֶב
sources.says: Rashi says Israel in turn swapped their craft for that of the nations, who come with the sword.

31:21.headline: Eleazar teaches the law because Moses, angry, forgot it
31:21.body: Here Eleazar the priest teaches the law, not Moses. Rashi says Moses had grown angry at the officers, and anger made him forget the rules for cleaning gentile vessels, just as anger led him to strike the rock.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁבָּא מֹשֶׁה לִכְלַל כַּעַס בָּא לִכְלַל טָעוּת, שֶׁנִּתְעַלְּמוּ מִמֶּנּוּ הִלְכוֹת גִּעוּלֵי גּוֹיִם
sources.says: Rashi says because Moses came to anger, he came to error: the laws of purging gentile vessels slipped from him.

sources.quote: וְכֵן בְּשִׁמְעוּ נָא הַמֹּרִים (במדבר כ') "וַיַּךְ אֶת הַסֶּלַע" — עַל יְדֵי הַכַּעַס טָעָה
sources.says: Rashi says the same happened at 'Listen, you rebels', when Moses struck the rock: through anger he erred.

31:22.headline: 'Only' the metal: scrape off the rust first
31:22.body: אך usually means 'only' or 'but'. Rashi says it limits using the vessels until they are purged, and the sages read it as 'only the bare metal', so the rust must come off before purging.

sources.quote: וְ"אַךְ" לְשׁוֹן מִעוּט, כְּלוֹמַר מְמֻעָטִין אַתֶּם מִלְּהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בַּכֵּלִים אֲפִלּוּ לְאַחַר טָהֲרָתָן מִטֻּמְאַת הַמֵּת
sources.says: Rashi says אך is a limiting word: you are held back from using the vessels even after they are cleansed of corpse impurity.

sources.quote: שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַעֲבִיר חֲלוּדָה שֶׁלּוֹ קֹדֶם שֶׁיַּגְעִילֶנּוּ, וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן אך, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא שָׁם חֲלוּדָה אַךְ הַמַּתֶּכֶת יִהְיֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the sages learn that rust must be removed before purging: 'only' the metal as it is, with no rust.

31:23.headline: 'Water of niddah': ash water, or a ritual bath?
31:23.body: מי נדה usually means the water mixed with red heifer ash. Ibn Ezra says that is how it looks to him, but the sages read it as enough water for a woman's ritual bath, and he defers to them.

sources.quote: היה נראה לנו כי הוא מי אפר הפרה כמו מי נדה לא זורק עליו וחז"ל אמרו כי טעמו בשיעור המים שתרחץ בהם האשה הנדה ודעתם רחבה מדעתינו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it seemed to mean the red heifer's ash water, but the sages said it means the amount of water a niddah bathes in, and their knowledge is wider than ours.

sources.quote: וּמֵי נִדָּה הַכְּתוּבִין כָּאן דָּרְשׁוּ מַיִם הָרְאוּיִם לִטְבֹּל בָּהֶם נִדָּה, וְכַמָּה הֵם? אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read 'niddah water' here as water fit for a niddah to immerse in, which is forty se'ah.

31:49.headline: 'Not one man missing': lost in battle, or lost to sin
31:49.body: נפקד here means 'was missing', not 'was counted', as Rashi shows from other verses. Ramban adds that the sages also read it as: not one of us slipped away to sin.

sources.quote: ולא נפקד. לֹא נֶחְסַר, וְתַרְגּוּמוֹ "לָא שְׁגָא", אַף הוּא בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִי חִסָּרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'none was lacking', and the Aramaic translation also uses a word for lacking.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ (שבת סד) ״וְלֹא נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ״ - לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה
sources.says: Ramban says the sages read 'not one man of us was missing' as referring to sin.

31:50.headline: An unknown ornament, read as jewelry for the womb
31:50.body: Ibn Ezra treats כומז as just another piece of jewelry. Rashi says it was an ornament shaped like the womb, and the gift atoned for the soldiers' thoughts about the women of Midian.

sources.quote: דְּפוּס שֶׁל בֵּית הָרֶחֶם, לְכַפֵּר הִרְהוּר הַלֵּב שֶׁל בְּנוֹת מִדְיָן
sources.says: Rashi says it was a mold of the womb, brought to atone for the heart's thoughts about the daughters of Midian.

sources.quote: וכומז. כחביריו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like the items listed with it.

4:22.headline: 'Lift the head' means count, and also raise up
4:22.body: נשא את ראש, 'lift the head', is a way of saying 'count'. Kli Yakar and Or HaChaim note it is used for Kohath and Gershon but not for Merari, because lifting the head also means raising someone's rank.

sources.quote: ונאמר לשון נשא בבני קהת ובבני גרשון, ולא בבני מררי, לפי שהיה לשניהם מעלה ביתר שאת על בני מררי
sources.says: Kli Yakar says the word נשא is used for Kohath and Gershon, not Merari, because both had higher standing than Merari.

sources.quote: שינשא וירומם בני גרשון לערך בני מררי
sources.says: Or HaChaim says the word means God raised Gershon above Merari.

4:47.headline: 'The work of work': music for the offerings
4:47.body: עבדת עבדה, 'the work of work', is an odd phrase. Rashi and Bahya say it is the Levites' music, a service that goes with another service, the offerings, while Chizkuni says it is taking down and putting up the Tabernacle.

sources.quote: עבדת עבדה. היא השיר במצלתים וכנורות, שהיא עבודה לעבודה אחרת
sources.says: Rashi says it is the song with cymbals and harps, a service for another service.

sources.quote: זה השיר שהיה עבודה לעבודה אחרת והיא הקרבנות
sources.says: Bahya says it is the song, which served another service, the offerings.

sources.quote: לעבד עבדת עבדה הורדת והקמת המשכן
sources.says: Chizkuni says it means taking down and putting up the Tabernacle.

5:12.headline: Straying from the path, and a spirit of folly
5:12.body: Plainly תשטה means the wife turns aside from modest ways, but the sages hear שטות, folly, in it: no one commits adultery unless a spirit of folly enters them. Kli Yakar even hears תשתה, 'she drinks', since ט and ת can swap.

sources.quote: אין המנאפין נואפין עד שתכנס בהן רוח שטות, דכתיב "כי תשטה"
sources.says: Rashi quotes the sages that adulterers do not sin until a spirit of folly enters them, reading it from תשטה.

sources.quote: ופשוטו של מקרא: כי תשטה — תט מדרכי צניעות
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is that she turns aside from modest ways.

sources.quote: כי ״תשטה״ בטי״ת כמו ״תשתה״ בתי״ו
sources.says: Kli Yakar suggests that תשטה with a ט is like תשתה, 'she drinks', with a ת.

5:13.headline: 'Not caught', or 'not forced'?
5:13.body: נתפשה can mean 'caught' or 'seized'. Ibn Ezra reads 'she was not caught' by witnesses, while Rashi and Rashbam read 'she was not forced', so the law covers only a willing act.

sources.quote: נתפשה. נאנסה, כמו "ותפשה ושכב עמה"
sources.says: Rashi says the word means forced, as in the verse about a man who seizes a girl.

sources.quote: והיא לא נתפשה - לא נאנסה
sources.says: Rashbam says it means she was not forced.

sources.quote: והיא לא נתפשה. בעדים אנשים או על ידי נשים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means she was not caught by witnesses, men or women.

5:14.headline: Not just jealousy, but a formal warning
5:14.body: וקנא sounds like 'he was jealous'. Rashi and Sforno say the sages read it as a warning: the husband tells his wife not to be alone with a certain man.

sources.quote: פרשו רבותינו לשון התראה, שמתרה בה, אל תסתרי עם איש פלוני
sources.says: Rashi says the sages explain it as a warning: he warns her not to be alone with a certain man.

sources.quote: וקנא את אשתו. התרה בה ואמר: אל תסתרי עם איש פלוני
sources.says: Sforno says it means he warned her not to be alone with a certain man.

5:15.headline: No incense, because the mothers are called incense
5:15.body: Most grain offerings carry לבנה, frankincense, but this one does not. Rashi says the Matriarchs are called 'the hill of frankincense' in the Song of Songs, and this woman turned from their ways.

sources.quote: שהאמהות נקראו לבונה, שנאמר "ואל גבעת הלבונה"
sources.says: Rashi says the Matriarchs are called frankincense, from the verse 'to the hill of frankincense'.

sources.quote: והיא פרשה מדרכיהן
sources.says: Rashi says this woman turned away from their ways.

5:21.headline: Her name becomes the words of an oath
5:21.body: What does it mean to become 'a curse and an oath'? Rashi and Rashbam say people will use her story when they curse or swear: 'may it happen to me as it happened to her'.

sources.quote: שיהיו הכל נשבעין ביך
sources.says: Rashi says everyone will swear by her.

sources.quote: שאם תכזב בי תהיה מקולל, כאשה פלונית שצבתה בטנה ונפלה ירכה
sources.says: Rashbam says a person will make another swear: if you lie, may you be cursed like the woman whose belly swelled.

5:21.headline: The thigh, or the womb?
5:21.body: ירך usually means thigh, but Chizkuni says here it means the womb, as in 'those who came out of Jacob's ירך'. Rashi notes the curse names it before the belly, because the sin began there.

sources.quote: ירכך היא בית הרחם דוגמא תחת ירכי יוצאי ירך יעקב
sources.says: Chizkuni says the word means the womb, as in 'those who came out of Jacob's thigh'.

sources.quote: בקללה הקדים ירך לבטן, לפי שבה התחילה בעברה תחלה
sources.says: Rashi says the curse names the thigh before the belly because the sin started with it.

6:2.headline: Yafli: to set oneself apart, or to do something wondrous
6:2.body: Rashi and Onkelos read יפלא as 'set apart'. Ibn Ezra adds a second sense from פלא, 'wonder': taking this vow is remarkable, since most people follow their desires.

sources.quote: כי יפלא. יַפְרִישׁ
sources.says: Rashi says yafli means 'sets apart'.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי יְפָרֵשׁ לְמִדַּר נְדַר נְזִירוּ
sources.says: Onkelos renders: when he sets himself apart to vow a nazirite vow.

sources.quote: יפלא. יפריש או יעשה דבר פלא כי רוב העולם הולכים אחר תאותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means sets apart, or does a wondrous thing, since most of the world follows its desires.

6:3.headline: Shechar: any strong drink, or simply old wine?
6:3.body: Rashi follows Onkelos, 'new wine and old', since wine makes one drunk when it is old. Ibn Ezra also brings the view that שכר is anything that makes a person drunk.

sources.quote: מֵחֲמַר חֲדַת וְעַתִּיק יִזַּר
sources.says: Onkelos renders: from new wine and old he shall abstain.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַיַּיִן מְשַׁכֵּר כְּשֶׁהוּא יָשָׁן
sources.says: Rashi says wine intoxicates when it is old.

sources.quote: ואחרים אמרו שכר ממש כל דבר שישתכר האדם ממנו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says others hold that shechar is anything a person gets drunk from.

6:3.headline: Mishrat: a word found only here, grapes soaked or loosened
6:3.body: Rashi says משרת means soaking in water or any drink, as the Mishnah speaks of a nazir who soaked his bread in wine. Rashbam takes it as whatever comes loose and falls from the grapes, like a man freed from his chains.

sources.quote: משרת. אין לו חבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner elsewhere.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן צְבִיעָה בְּמַיִם וְכָל מַשְׁקֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it means steeping in water or any liquid.

sources.quote: נָזִיר שֶׁשָּׁרָה פִתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi cites the Mishnah: a nazir who soaked his bread.

sources.quote: כל מה שנבדל ונופל מן הענבים, כאדם הנבדל וניתר מקשר הכבלים והזיקים שקשור בהם
sources.says: Rashbam says it is whatever separates and falls from the grapes, like a man released from the chains that bound him.

6:4.headline: Chartzanim: the seeds, or the skins?
6:4.body: Both חרצנים and זג appear only in this verse. Rashi says חרצנים are the seeds; Ibn Ezra reports commentators who had it the other way round.

sources.quote: חרצנים. הֵם הַגַּרְעִינִין
sources.says: Rashi says chartzanim are the seeds.

sources.quote: מחרצנים. אין לו ריע וכן זג והמפרשים אמרו חרצנים חצונים וזג פנימי' ואחרים הפכו הפירוש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says neither word has a partner; the commentators said chartzanim are the outer part and zag the inner, and others reversed it.

sources.quote: ומלת חרצנים אין לה חבר בכל המקרא, וכן מלת זג
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says neither chartzanim nor zag appears anywhere else in Scripture.

6:7.headline: Nezer: the crown of his God on his head
6:7.body: Onkelos renders נזר as a crown: 'the crown of his God is on his head'. Ibn Ezra and Rabbeinu Bahya draw the lesson: the true king is the one free of his desires, while other people are their slaves.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי כְּלִילָא דֶאֱלָהֵיהּ עַל רֵישֵׁיהּ
sources.says: Onkelos renders: for the crown of his God is on his head.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים כי מלת נזיר מגזרת נזר והעד כי נזר אלהיו על ראשו ואיננו רחוק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some derive nazir from nezer, crown, citing this verse, and that this is not far-fetched.

sources.quote: והמלך באמת שיש לו נזר ועטרת מלכות בראשו כל מי שהוא חפשי מן התאות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the true king, with a royal crown on his head, is anyone free of desires.

sources.quote: ונקרא בשם הזה על שם שהוא מלך מולך על התאוות הפך משאר בני העולם שהם עבדי התאוות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says he is called so because he rules over his desires, unlike others who are their slaves.

6:9.headline: Petha pitom: an accident, a mistake, or even on purpose?
