6:9.body: Rashi reads פתע as an accident beyond one's control and פתאום as an honest mistake, though some say the two words mean one thing. Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis who read פתאם as on purpose, from פתאים, 'fools'.

sources.quote: בפתע. זֶה אֹנֶס
sources.says: Rashi says petha means something forced, beyond his control.

sources.quote: פתאום. זֶה שׁוֹגֵג, וְיֵ"א פֶּתַע פִּתְאֹם דָּבָר אֶחָד הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says pitom means by mistake, and some say petha pitom is one thing.

sources.quote: נאמר בנזיר בפתע שהוא שוגג, פתאם הוא מזיד, לפי שנאמר (משלי כב) ופתאים עברו ונענשו
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis: petha is by mistake and pitom is on purpose, from 'fools pass on and are punished'.

6:11.headline: How did the nazir 'sin against his soul'?
6:11.body: Rashi gives the plain sense: he was not careful to avoid the dead. He also cites Rabbi Elazar HaKappar: his sin was making himself suffer by giving up wine.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא נִזְהַר מִטֻּמְאַת הַמֵּת
sources.says: Rashi says he was not careful about impurity from the dead.

sources.quote: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר אוֹמֵר, שֶׁצִּעֵר עַצְמוֹ מִן הַיַּיִן
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Elazar HaKappar: he caused himself pain by keeping from wine.

sources.quote: על הנפש. הוא על נפש מת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'the soul' here means a dead body.

6:14.headline: Why a sin offering for finishing a holy vow?
6:14.body: Ramban says the nazir 'sins' by ending his term, because he steps down from holiness; he ought to have stayed a nazir all his life. Rabbeinu Bahya says even so the law is unusual, since no other offering is brought for something still to come.

sources.quote: כִּי הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה חוֹטֵא נַפְשׁוֹ בִּמְלֹאת הַנְּזִירוּת, כִּי הוּא עַתָּה נָזוֹר מִקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ וַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם
sources.says: Ramban says this man sins against himself when his term ends, for he now turns away from his holiness and God's service.

sources.quote: וְרָאוּי הָיָה לוֹ שֶׁיַּזִּיר לְעוֹלָם
sources.says: Ramban says he should rightly have stayed a nazir forever.

sources.quote: ועם כל הטעם הזה לא יצא קרבנו של נזיר מן החדוש כי היכן מצינו קרבן על העתיד
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says that even with this reason the offering stays unique, for where else is an offering brought for the future?

6:23.headline: Ko, 'thus': the manner of the blessing, and the number 25
6:23.body: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis: 'thus' (כה) fixes the manner, with raised hands, in Hebrew, standing, aloud, face to face, and with God's Name. He adds that כה has the value 25: the blessing joins the priests' 24 gifts.

sources.quote: ודרשו רז"ל כה תברכו בנשיאות כפים, כה תברכו בלשון הקדש, כה תברכו בעמידה, כה תברכו בקול רם, כה תברכו פנים כנגד פנים, כה תברכו בשם המפורש
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the rabbis: bless with raised hands, in the holy tongue, standing, aloud, face to face, and with the explicit Name.

sources.quote: ולפי שעתיד למסור להם ארבעה ועשרים מתנות כהונה ועם זו הם עשרים וחמשה, לכך הזכיר הלשון הזה כ"ה תברכו
sources.says: He says that since the priests would receive 24 gifts, and with this one they make 25, the Torah says 'ko', which equals 25.

6:23.headline: Amor, spelled in full: bless with a whole heart
6:23.body: Rashi notes that אמור is written in full. The midrash he cites learns that the priests must not bless in a rush, but with intent and a whole heart; he adds that all the people must be able to hear.

sources.quote: אמור. מָלֵא — לֹא תְבָרְכֵם בְּחִפָּזוֹן וּבַהֲלוּת, אֶלָּא בְכַוָּנָה וּבְלֵב שָׁלֵם
sources.says: Rashi says amor is spelled full: do not bless them hastily, but with intent and a whole heart.

sources.quote: אמור להם. שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֻלָּם שׁוֹמְעִים
sources.says: Rashi says 'say to them' means so that all can hear.

6:24.headline: A blessing no robber can take
6:24.body: Rashi says a human giver cannot protect his gift from thieves, but God both gives and guards. Ibn Ezra reads it the same way: He keeps what He added, so no one takes it.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַנּוֹתֵן מַתָּנָה לְעַבְדּוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְשָׁמְרוֹ מִכָּל אָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says one who gives his servant a gift cannot guard it from everyone.

sources.quote: אֲבָל הַקָּבָּ"ה, הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן, הוּא הַשּׁוֹמֵר
sources.says: Rashi says God is both the giver and the guard.

sources.quote: וטעם וישמרך. שישמור התוספת שלא יגזול אחר מה שהוסיף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says He will guard the added good so that no one robs it.

6:25.headline: 'May He shine His face': a smile, or His Presence's light?
6:25.body: Rashi reads it as a warm, smiling face turned toward you. Onkelos, and Ramban citing Rabbi Natan, read it as the light of God's Presence shining on you.

sources.quote: יַרְאֶה לְךָ פָּנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת, פָּנִים צְהֻבּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says He will show you a smiling, bright face.

sources.quote: יַנְהַר יְיָ שְׁכִנְתֵּיהּ לְוָתָךְ
sources.says: Onkelos renders: may the Lord make His Presence shine toward you.

sources.quote: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: זֶה מְאוֹר שְׁכִינָה
sources.says: Ramban cites Rabbi Natan: this is the light of the Divine Presence.

6:26.headline: 'May He lift His face': calm His anger, or watch over you?
6:26.body: Rashi reads it as 'may He hold back His anger', and Maimonides says 'face' here means God's care staying with us. Rashbam squares it with 'who shows no favor' (Deuteronomy 10:17): God does not excuse sin, but turns toward the one He loves.

sources.quote: ישא ה' פניו אליך. יִכְבֹּשׁ כַּעֲסוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means He will suppress His anger.

sources.quote: פנים הוא גם שם החסות וההשגחה
sources.says: Maimonides says 'face' is also a word for protection and providence.

sources.quote: והכוונה להתלוות השגחתו עלינו
sources.says: He says the verse means that God's providence will accompany us.

sources.quote: הקב"ה לא ישא פני איש לנקותו מכל פשעיו, אבל הוא ישא פנים שלו את אהובו שיפנה אליו לחננו
sources.says: Rashbam says God will not show favor to clear a person of all his sins, but will lift His own face to the one He loves, turning to be gracious to him.

6:27.headline: 'And I will bless them': Israel, or the priests?
6:27.body: Rashi gives both readings: God blesses Israel, agreeing with the priests, or God blesses the priests themselves. Ibn Ezra holds that 'them' means everyone, priests and Israel alike.

sources.quote: לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאַסְכִּים עִם הַכֹּהֲנִים; דָּ"אַ, וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם — לַכֹּהֲנִים
sources.says: Rashi says: I will bless Israel and agree with the priests; another reading, I will bless the priests.

sources.quote: לפי דעתי שמ"ם אברכם סימן לכלם כהנים וישראלים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says in his view 'them' refers to all of them, priests and Israelites.

sources.quote: כשיברכו הכהנים לישראל בשמי ולא בשמם, אני אברכם לישראל
sources.says: Rashbam says when the priests bless Israel in God's name and not their own, God blesses Israel.
